results.input: Disclosure, advertising, anti-fraud, and educational-content boundaries relevant to publishing capital-formation, private-company, and investment-adjacent editorial content

output.confidence: High — findings are grounded in official SEC staff guidance, FINRA regulatory reports, and industry legal analysis as of September 1, 2026.
output.current_findings: As of September 1, 2026, the SEC’s Division of Investment Management has updated its Marketing Rule FAQs to mandate the use of model fees in performance advertising when anticipated fees exceed historical actual fees (Observed). FINRA’s 2026 Annual Regulatory Oversight Report identifies Generative AI (GenAI) as a primary risk vector, requiring firms to implement detection for AI-enabled fraud and deepfakes in public communications (Observed). The regulatory boundary between "educational content" and "solicitation" increasingly relies on the absence of specific security recommendations, with FINRA proposing Rule 2210 modernizations in July 2026 to facilitate post-use review for neutral market commentary (Observed). SEC examination priorities for 2026 specifically target the integrity of testimonials and endorsements within VC-owned media channels like podcasts and newsletters (Observed). Enforcement trends in 2026 further highlight "shadow solicitation," where editorial dossiers are scrutinized if they function as primary funnels for private fund offerings without adequate disclosure (Inference).
output.editorial_implications: A Human Blockchain capital-layer strategy should prioritize systemic architecture and market mechanics over specific private company performance to maintain a clear "educational" status. All editorial content must feature prominent disclaimers stating the non-solicitation nature of the information and the absence of investment recommendations. The use of AI for content generation requires a documented "Human-in-the-Loop" review process to comply with 2026 anti-fraud and GenAI disclosure mandates. Adopting "post-use review" protocols for educational blogs can accelerate content cycles while remaining compliant with FINRA's modernized communication standards.
